name: Sharing the Land
summary: In Mulgore, Baine Bloodhoof calls you to stop Palemane gnolls from killing the plains' wildlife. By striking their hunters, you help protect the herds and the tauren way of living with the Earth Mother.

sections.title: A Land Out of Balance
sections.body: The tauren take from the land only what they need and honor the Earth Mother in all things. Palemane gnolls have settled south of Bloodhoof Village and in a cavern to the west, where they slaughter wildlife across the plains. Their hunting leaves carcasses behind and harms the balance of the grasslands. The tauren are building a peaceful home in Mulgore, but the gnolls' wasteful killing threatens it.

sections.title: When Words Fail
sections.body: Baine Bloodhoof tried to speak with the Palemane gnolls and settle the matter peacefully. They rejected every attempt and kept killing wildlife. Now Baine sends young braves to their hunting camps to put down the poachers, tanners, and skinners before the grasslands suffer lasting harm.

sections.title: The Circle of Life and Death
sections.body: When you return, Baine teaches that taking life is never for malice, but may be needed to keep harmony. Life and death form a circle, and every guardian of Mulgore must carry that truth.

faq.answer: Baine Bloodhoof, son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, gives you this work in Bloodhoof Village, in central Mulgore.

faq.q: Why are the tauren targeting the Palemane gnolls?
faq.answer: The Palemane gnolls hunt Mulgore's wildlife recklessly and deplete the herds. They also rejected the tauren's attempts to speak peacefully.
The Palemanes camp south of Bloodhoof Village and live in the Palemane Rock cave system to the west.

faq.q: Did the tauren try to make peace first?
faq.answer: Yes. Baine says the tauren tried several times to speak with the gnolls and share the land, but the Palemanes rejected their peaceful offers.

faq.q: What lesson is Baine trying to teach here?
faq.answer: Baine wants young defenders to understand that life and death form an unbreakable circle. Taking life may be needed to protect the balance, but it must be done with respect for the Earth Mother.
The Palemane gnolls are a primitive, hyena-like tribe native to Mulgore. They have pale fur, defend their territory aggressively, and disregard the harmony of the plains.

angles.text: As a young tauren, answering Baine's call teaches you to defend Mulgore and honor the Earth Mother's balance.
The Palemane skinners and poachers hunt with cruelty and waste, without a true hunter's respect for wild creatures.
As a druid, you know unchecked poaching harms the spirit of the plains, and the land's harmony needs your help.
As a member of the Horde, helping Baine Bloodhoof strengthens your bond with the leaders of the young tauren nation.
